issues.description: Method SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(): Problem statement (UML and textual description) declares checkOrderReady() with a void return type, but the solution implementation defines public boolean checkOrderReady(). This mismatch leaves students unsure which signature to implement (a void method with only side-effects, or a boolean-returning method) and whether their implementation should return a value. The ambiguity can cause compilation/test differences if automated tests expect the void signature described in the problem.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent between the specification and the code. Prefer option A to match the problem description: change the implementation signature in SealSaloon to public void checkOrderReady() and remove the boolean return value (keep the same internal logic of serving orders and printing). Alternatively, if the boolean return is intentional (indicating whether any order was served), update the problem statement/UML to declare checkOrderReady(): boolean and document the meaning of the returned value. Ensure tests and template code (if any) use the chosen signature.
